title: Event Horizon: a black hole drawn from the measured Page curve
made_with: Blender 5 (EEVEE) from problems/event-horizon results (N = 26 evaporation on the A100)
caption: Artwork from data, not an astrophysical image. Each ring of the accretion disk is one evaporation step of the 26-qubit sequential-evaporation run; its glow is the measured mean radiation entropy S(R) at that step, so the disk brightens toward the Page time and fades as the hole evaporates.

title: Three-body braid: an equal-mass candidate orbit through time
made_with: Blender 5 (EEVEE), real trajectory re-integrated with DOP853
caption: Candidate 14 (m1 = m2 = m3 = 1, T = 45.872): the three bodies' paths over one full period, with time running left to right. A verified periodic orbit whose topological family is absent from the 2,060 catalogued orbits checked (candidate, not proven new).

title: Three-body: 16 candidate periodic-orbit families
caption: 17 verified periodic orbits in 16 topological families (return error < 1e-8, two tolerances agree) absent from the 2,060 catalogued orbits checked (Suvakov-Dmitrasinovic 2013, Li-Liao 2017, Li-Jing-Liao 2018); two at equal masses. Candidates, not proven new: later catalogs were not checked. m1 = m2 = 1, m3 in {0.5, 1, 2}.

title: The Lattice: 150 points, 116 lines to go
caption: Snapshot of our live no-three-in-line search on the 75x75 grid (SAT model rot180-150, seed 11, round 63, taken 06:32 PT, Nov 15). The 150 chosen points glow as pillars; red threads join chosen points that are still collinear (116 violated lines). Amber pillars sit on 4 or more violated lines: the solver's hot spots. Record to beat: 148 (Thomas-Prellberg).

title: Lattice orbit
made_with: Blender 5.2 EEVEE (script by GPT-6 Astra), FFMPEG H.264
caption: 8-second seamless camera orbit around the same live SAT snapshot (SAT model rot180-150, seed 11, round 63, taken 06:32 PT, Nov 15): 150 points, 116 violated lines. The model is 180-degree symmetric, so the view repeats every half turn.

title: Hadamard City
caption: The record 51x51 +-1 matrix (log10|det| = 43.3375, kgrey) extruded as a city: the 1296 +1 entries are cyan-roofed towers, the 1305 -1 entries low amber plinths (mostly hidden between towers at this angle); tower height follows the mean sign of each 5x5 neighbourhood.

title: Snake in the 13-cube
caption: The record 2950-edge snake-in-the-box (kgrey), verified and linearly projected from 13 dimensions to 3: rarely flipped coordinates become long bridges, frequent ones local wiggles. Colour runs amber (start) to cyan (end); faint dust marks all 8192 cube vertices.

title: Snake turntable
made_with: Blender 5.2 EEVEE (script by GPT-6 Astra), FFMPEG H.264
caption: The same 2950-edge snake rotating once about its vertical axis.

title: Phoenixastar banner
caption: Built only from the run's own data: the live 75 x 75 no-three-in-line SAT model and two of the verified three-body candidate orbits, re-integrated from their initial conditions.

title: Three-body: the figure-eight, rediscovered
caption: Correctness check for the new astrophysics problem (periodic orbits of the Newtonian three-body problem). Our GPU search (300,000 random initial velocities, batched Levenberg-Marquardt) converged on Moore's figure-eight: vx=0.3471168902, vy=0.5327249445, T=6.3259139921, return error 7.0e-10 in the official float64 verifier. Rediscovery of a known orbit (Moore 1993; Chenciner-Montgomery 2000).

title: Three-body: Moth II
caption: Rediscovery of the 'moth II' orbit of Suvakov and Dmitrasinovic (2013): equal masses, T=28.6693, return error 1.6e-11. Found by the same GPU test run (seed 0, 300,000 seeds, periods 5 to 30) and matched to the literature catalog by initial condition and period.

title: Three-body: a k=5 satellite of the figure-eight
caption: Equal masses, vx=0.1388980233, vy=0.5375024150, T=23.3346, return error 9.6e-12. Its topological word is the fifth power of the figure-eight word, so the verifier files it under the figure-eight family (a 'topological-power satellite', a known phenomenon: Suvakov 2014), not as a new family.

title: Three-body: candidate orbit at m3 = 1.5 (not in our catalog)
caption: Unequal masses (m1=m2=1, m3=1.5): vx=0.3971945789, vy=0.8898238352, T=22.50016117, return error 4.7e-12 (confirmed independently with scipy DOP853: 8.8e-12). Its topological word matches none of the 2060 literature orbits we checked (Suvakov-Dmitrasinovic 2013, Li-Liao 2017, Li-Jing-Liao 2018). CANDIDATE only: the later catalogs (Li-Li-Liao 2021, Hristov et al. 2021-2024) were not checked and no multi-precision confirmation was run.

title: Three-body: second candidate at m3 = 1.5
caption: m1=m2=1, m3=1.5: vx=0.0448250, vy=0.8108540, T=13.4697, return error 4.9e-11 in the official verifier. Passes within 0.012 of a two-body collision. Not in our 2060-orbit catalog; candidate only, same caveats as the previous image.

title: Three-body: the 7 families of the first GPU test
caption: One orbit per topological family verified in the first test run (equal masses, periods 5 to 30, 300,000 seeds, about 4 minutes on one A100), ordered by period: butterfly I, figure-eight, yin-yang I, moth I, dragonfly, Li-Liao I.A-4 and moth II. All 7 are known families; the run found 0 new ones, as expected in the region Li and Liao scanned exhaustively.
